articles.title: Waste bulrush transformed into copper-enhanced material for dye removal from wastewater
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Industrial activities such as textile manufacturing, paper production, leather processing and food processing can generate wastewater containing synthetic dyes. Because many synthetic dyes are chemically stable, difficult to biodegrade and environmentally persistent, their release into waterways can pose risks to aquatic ecosystems and human health.

articles.title: Astronomers discover a radio galaxy with evidence of four separate jet outbursts
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Astronomers have identified what may be the first example of a new class of radio galaxy, one whose central black hole appears to have launched powerful jets on four separate occasions. High-resolution observations with the upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT), combined with data from MeerKAT and the Very Large Array, reveal four pairs of radio structures arranged symmetrically around the central galaxy.

articles.title: Glucosamine, a popular joint supplement, linked to faster Alzheimer’s progression
articles.summary: A large health-record analysis found that glucosamine use was associated with a 25% higher likelihood of mild cognitive impairment progressing to dementia. Lab experiments suggest the popular joint supplement may intensify an abnormal sugar-tagging process in the Alzheimer’s brain, although researchers say clinical trials are needed to determine whether it actually causes harm.

articles.title: DNA reveals chemosynthesis genes in bacteria living on coral reef fish gills
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Chemosynthetic bacteria have been documented in various marine environments and in association with invertebrate hosts such as annelid worms and mollusks, but their presence in fish appears to be a new discovery. The findings show that fish gills host a complex and specialized microbiome that is not yet well understood but could play an important role in fish metabolism, immunity and health.

articles.title: Why rheumatoid arthritis pain may persist even when inflammation is under control
articles.summary: Pain and fatigue in rheumatoid arthritis can persist even after inflammation improves, with depression, poor sleep, obesity, smoking, and chronic pain potentially helping sustain symptoms. Researchers say identifying these hidden drivers could prevent unnecessary medication changes and lead to more personalized treatment.
